structure.title: Choose a business structure
structure.subtitle: Sole proprietorship · partnership · corporation
structure.priority.name: One name across Canada
structure.why.sole: The simplest way to start: you and the business are the same, and profits go on your personal tax return.
structure.why.partnership: Easy to form with your co-owners. Put your agreement in writing: general partners share the liability equally unless it says otherwise.
structure.why.corporation: A separate legal entity: shareholders aren’t responsible for its debts, and it can sell shares to raise money.
structure.why.federal: Incorporating federally ({fee} online) protects your name across Canada.
structure.why.provincial: You can incorporate federally ({fee} online) or with your province.
structure.sole.liability: You’re personally responsible, even with your personal property
structure.sole.tax: Profit goes on your personal return (Form T2125)
structure.sole.setup: Usually register with your province or territory (not always needed under your own name); fees vary
structure.sole.life: Stops existing when the owner dies
structure.partnership.owners: Two or more people, corporations or trusts
structure.partnership.liability: General partners share the liability equally, unless an agreement says otherwise. The partnership is bound by each partner’s actions in the usual course of business
structure.partnership.tax: Each partner reports their share; the partnership itself files no income tax return
structure.partnership.setup: Usually register with your province or territory; a written agreement is wise
structure.partnership.life: Stops existing when an owner dies
structure.corporation.owners: Shareholders (one person can be the only one)
structure.corporation.liability: Shareholders aren’t responsible for its debts (lenders may ask for a personal guarantee)
structure.corporation.tax: Files its own T2 return within 6 months of year‑end
structure.corporation.life: Continues until it’s wound up, amalgamated or gives up its charter
structure.corporation.money: Can sell shares or bonds to investors, and can borrow at lower rates
structure.handoff.corporationNote: See the 5 steps to incorporate federally, then file online.
structure.handoff.registerNote: Find your provincial or territorial business registry.
structure.ask.register: Do I need to register for GST/HST?
structure.ask.register.label: Check GST/HST
structure.footnote: A simple rule of thumb from official information, not legal or tax advice. For your own situation, talk to a lawyer or accountant.
inc.title: Federal incorporation planner
inc.subtitle: Corporations Canada · Canada Business Corporations Act
inc.hero.standard: You can be incorporated in 1 business day
inc.hero.express: You can be incorporated in 4 hours
inc.hero.sub: Filed online. Your business number arrives by email within minutes.
inc.express.desc: Express service: {fee} more, done in 4 hours
inc.name: Corporate name
inc.name.numberedNote: Simplest: Corporations Canada assigns the number. You can still do business under another name.
inc.name.wordNote: Once approved, you have the right to use it across Canada. The name search is built into the online application: no Nuans report needed.
inc.step1.title: 1. Name your corporation
inc.step1.numbered: Choose a numbered name, assigned for you.
inc.step1.word: Pick a word name; it’s checked during your application.
inc.step2.title: 2. Create your articles of incorporation
inc.step3.title: 3. Set your registered office and first directors
inc.step3.detail: Your registered office is where you must keep your corporate records and where official documents will be served. You also need at least one director aged 18 or older; one person can be the only shareholder, director and officer.
inc.step4.title: 4. File your individuals with significant control
inc.step4.detail: Who owns and controls the corporation.
inc.step5.title: 5. Submit and pay {fee}
inc.step5.detail: Online through the Online Filing Centre. You get an email with your business number within minutes of incorporating.
inc.where.hint: A federal corporation must also register in each province or territory where it does business.
inc.where.none: Choose one or more provinces or territories to see how to register there.
inc.route.bundled.detail: The provincial forms are completed with the information you give when you incorporate. Confirm with the province.
inc.route.partner: Register online through Corporations Canada’s partner service
inc.route.partner.detail: A faster, shared registration after you incorporate.
inc.route.registrar: Register with the provincial or territorial registry
inc.route.registrar.detail: Visit that registry’s website after you incorporate.
inc.where.fees: Most provinces and territories charge a fee to register; it varies.
inc.after.bn: Your business number and corporation income tax account come automatically.
inc.after.gst: Register for GST/HST or payroll with the CRA if you need them.
inc.after.annual: File an annual return with Corporations Canada every year ({fee} online).
inc.after.t2: File a T2 corporation income tax return within 6 months of your year‑end, even if you owe nothing.
inc.handoff.note: You’ll incorporate and pay in the Online Filing Centre.
reg.title: GST/HST and business number check
reg.subtitle: Small supplier test · Canada Revenue Agency
reg.hero.small: You don’t have to register for GST/HST yet
reg.hero.small.sub: You can sell {amount} more over these four quarters before you must register.
reg.hero.small.voluntary: You can still choose to register voluntarily.
reg.hero.quarter.sub: Your sales passed {threshold} in a single quarter ({quarter}). Charge GST/HST starting with the sale that put you over, and register within 29 days.
reg.hero.four.future: Your four-quarter total passed {threshold}. You stop being a small supplier on {date}; charge GST/HST from your first sale after that and register within 29 days.
reg.hero.four.pastLatest: Your four-quarter total passed {threshold}, so you stopped being a small supplier by {date} at the latest. Register and charge GST/HST from your first sale after that date.
reg.hero.must: Taxi and rideshare drivers must register
reg.hero.must.sub: You need a business number and a GST/HST account whatever you earn.
reg.hero.empty: Enter your sales to see if you must register
reg.hero.empty.sub: Use your taxable sales before expenses, from all your businesses, for each calendar quarter.
reg.meter.noLimit: The {amount} limit doesn’t apply to taxi and rideshare drivers.
reg.meter.sr: Sales over the last four quarters total {total}, against a {threshold} limit.
reg.quarter.label: Sales, {range}
reg.spread: We spread your {amount} a year evenly over these quarters, counting only the days so far this quarter. Replace these with your real sales.
reg.spread.young: Your {amount} for the year is spread evenly over the three quarters that have ended ({from} to {to}). This quarter has only just started{empty, select, yes {, so it is left empty} other {, so it counts only its first days}}. Replace these with your real sales.
reg.org.charityNote: Charities also have a {amount} gross revenue test. You’re a small supplier if you pass either test.
reg.accounts: What you need from the CRA
reg.bn.need: You need a 9-digit business number (BN). Each account adds a code to it, like 123456789 RT 0001.
reg.bn.optional: You don’t need a business number yet. You’ll get one when you open your first CRA account.
reg.bn.charity: Your charity already has a business number (its RR account). A GST/HST account is added to that same number.
reg.account.RT.detail: To charge, collect and send GST/HST.
reg.account.RP.detail: For employers, to send payroll deductions.
reg.account.RC.detail.noProvinceBn: Automatic with federal incorporation; otherwise register with the CRA.
reg.account.RM.detail: Opened with the CBSA in the CARM Client Portal.
reg.act.rideshare.desc: Uber, Lyft and taxis. Not food delivery.
reg.act.rideshare.orgHint: Businesses only: switching this on selects Business.
reg.rate.detail: When the sale happens in {province}. The rate depends on where you make the sale, not where you are.
reg.rate.pst: {province} also has a {rate}% provincial sales tax (PST). See the province’s website for it.
reg.quebec: If your business is located in Quebec, you register and file GST/HST with Revenu Québec, not the CRA.
reg.bnProvince: Registered your business with {province}? You may already have a business number.
reg.handoff.note: In Business Registration Online, choose Add account › Business account › Register a business.
reg.handoff.rqNote: Quebec businesses register for the GST and QST with Revenu Québec.
fund.title: Funding and support finder
fund.subtitle: Grants, loans and advice for your business
fund.need: What do you need help with?
fund.bbf.title: Business Benefits Finder
fund.bbf.body: Answer a few questions to get a personalized list of federal and provincial funding, loans and advice.
fund.agency.none: Choose your province or territory to see your federal regional development agency.
fund.agency.onChoose: In Ontario, it depends on where you are:
fund.program.csbfp.detail: Helps small businesses get loans from banks and credit unions by sharing the risk with lenders. Ask your financial institution.
fund.program.irap.detail: Advice, connections and funding to help small and medium-sized businesses innovate and take ideas to market.
fund.program.tcs.detail: Export advice, market information and contacts in over 160 cities worldwide.
fund.program.canadaStrong: Canada Strong: find support for your business
fund.program.canadaStrong.detail: Answer four questions to see the tariff-response programs that fit your need, region, size and sector.
fund.local.detail: {province}: local business development organizations and networks, listed on canada.ca.
fund.groups.detail: Indigenous businesses, social enterprises, co-operatives and veteran entrepreneurs.
fund.handoff.note: Business support and financing in every province and territory, including for Indigenous businesses, co-operatives and veterans.
fund.footnote: Programs, amounts and deadlines change often: each program’s page has the current details.
trade.title: Importing and exporting
trade.subtitle: Commercial goods · Canada Border Services Agency
trade.duty.hint: Find your rate in the Customs Tariff
trade.duty.unknown: Enter your duty rate to include customs duty.
trade.fx.off: Live exchange rates are unavailable right now. Enter the value in Canadian dollars.
trade.result.totalNoDuty: Add your duty rate to see the total.
trade.result.gstBeforeDuty: On the value only, before duty
trade.result.srNoDuty: GST on the value alone is {gst}, on a value for duty of {value}. Add your duty rate to see customs duty and the total.
trade.result.waiting: Enter the invoice amount to see the estimate.
trade.result.sr: Estimated duty {duty} and GST {gst}, for a total of {total} on a value for duty of {value}.
trade.estimate.note: An estimate. The CBSA uses the exchange rate on the date your goods are shipped, and other duties or taxes (such as excise taxes) may apply.
trade.tariffs: Some goods from the U.S. face Canadian counter-tariffs.
trade.tariffs.link: Complete list of U.S. products subject to counter-tariffs
trade.tariffs.other: Canada applies tariffs to some imports from the U.S. and other countries, such as steel and aluminum.
trade.import.s1: Create a CARM Client Portal account
trade.import.s2.d: Canadian businesses can get it in CARM. Non-residents get it from the CRA first.
trade.import.s3: Open an RM import program account
trade.import.s3.d: It turns your BN into a 15-character importer number, like 123456789 RM 0001.
trade.import.s4.d: Find the 10-digit tariff classification and duty rate, and declare the value in Canadian dollars.
trade.import.s5.d: Optional. Brokers are licensed by the CBSA but aren’t government, and charge fees. Release Prior to Payment is recommended if you use one.
trade.import.s6.d: Make a formal declaration to have your goods released, then pay duties and taxes.
trade.export.check: Do you need an export declaration?
trade.restricted: The goods are controlled, regulated or prohibited
trade.restricted.desc: They need an export permit, certificate or licence
trade.exp.reason.restricted: Controlled goods always need a permit, certificate or licence.
trade.exp.reason.restrictedUs: Controlled goods need a permit, certificate or licence, even to the U.S.
trade.exp.reason.us: Goods exported for use in the United States usually don’t need one. Goods moving through the U.S. to another country do.
trade.exp.reason.under: Goods that aren’t controlled and are worth less than {amount} don’t need one.
trade.exp.reason.over: Commercial goods worth {amount} or more going outside the U.S. need one.
trade.deadlines: When to report, by how the goods leave
trade.deadline.before: At least {count, plural, one {# hour} other {# hours}} before loading
trade.deadline.mail: At least {count, plural, one {# hour} other {# hours}} before it reaches the post office
trade.export.s1: Get a business number and RM export account
trade.export.s1.d: Through Exporter Program Enrolment in the CARM Client Portal.
trade.export.s2: Report with the Canadian Export Reporting System
trade.export.s2.d: Use the 8-digit Canadian Export Classification for your goods.
trade.export.s3: Keep your export records for {years} years
trade.export.s3.d: And give a certificate of origin when the buyer needs one.
trade.tcs: Export advice, market information and contacts in over 160 cities worldwide.
trade.handoff.importNote: The CBSA guide to importing commercial goods, step by step.
trade.handoff.exportNote: The CBSA exporters’ guide to reporting.
inc.step2.basic: Small private business? Basic incorporation gives you ready-made articles, one or two classes of shares, up to 10 directors and a numbered name. You can amend them later.
inc.step2.custom: With your own name, you customize your articles: your share structure and any limits on share transfers, the number of directors and any other provisions.
reg.hero.spread: Over {threshold} a year: you must register
reg.hero.spread.sub: At {amount} a year, you’re past the small supplier limit. Enter your real sales for each quarter to find the exact date you stopped being a small supplier.
fund.program.canexport.detail: Shares the costs of export activities to help businesses enter new international markets. The last intake closed on August 31, 2026: check the page for the next one.
fund.program.dutiesRelief.detail: Import goods without paying duties, as long as they’re eventually exported. From the Canada Border Services Agency.
fund.program.drawback.detail: Get back duties you paid on imported goods that you later export. From the Canada Border Services Agency.
trade.fx.offInvoice: Live exchange rates are unavailable right now. Convert your {amount} invoice to Canadian dollars and enter it here.
trade.exp.enter: Enter the shipment value to check
trade.exp.enter.sub: Commercial goods worth {amount} or more going outside the U.S. need an export declaration.
reg.sr.accounts.none: You don’t need a program account yet.
reg.hero.quarter.past: Your sales passed {threshold} in {quarter}, so you had to charge GST/HST from the sale that put you over and register within 29 days of it. Register now and give the CRA the date of that sale.
reg.hero.small.atLimit: You’re exactly at the {threshold} limit: your next taxable sale this quarter puts you over.
